content: Quaternium-15 is a chemical preservative commonly used in a wide range of cosmetic and industrial products. It functions by releasing formaldehyde, a known irritant and allergen. This compound is present in various consumer goods, including but not limited to mascara, eyeliner, moisturizers, lotions, shampoos, conditioners, nail polishes, personal lubricants, soaps, body washes, baby lotions or shampoos, facial cleansers, tanning oils, self-tanning creams, sunscreens, powders, shaving products, ointments, personal wipes or cleansers, as well as industrial products like wipes, paper, inks, paints, polishes, waxes, and industrial lubricants. Quaternium-15 has been identified as a potential cause of contact dermatitis, an inflammatory skin condition that arises as a result of an allergic reaction. This is particularly concerning for individuals with sensitive skin, infants, or when applied to sensitive areas of the body, such as the genital region. The chemical formula of Quaternium-15 is C9H16Cl2N4. This preservative is marketed under various names, including Dowicil 75, Dowicil 100, Dowco 184, Dowicide Q, 1-(3-Chloroallyl)-3,5,7-triaza-1-azoniaadamantane chloride, N-(3-chloroallyl)hexaminium chloride, hexamethylenetetramine chloroallyl chloride, 3,5,7-Triaza-1-azoniaadamantane, and 1-(3-chloroallyl)-chloride. Other preservatives that release formaldehyde and are chemically similar to Quaternium-15 include imidazolidinyl urea (marketed as Germall®), diazolidinyl urea (Germall II®), DMDM hydantoin (Glydant®), bronopol (Bronopol™), tris(hydroxymethyl)nitromethane (Tris Nitro®), and sodium hydroxymethylglycinate. Quaternium-15 is recognized as an allergen and has been associated with allergic contact dermatitis in susceptible individuals. Many people who are allergic to Quaternium-15 also exhibit sensitivity to formaldehyde. The presence of an allergy to Quaternium-15 can be confirmed through a diagnostic patch test.
